newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on index heavyweights.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on index heavyweights.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on modestly expanded volume on Monday with some index heavyweights traded actively, brokers said.

The B index rose 0.594 point or 0.80 percent to 74.384 on volume of 21.832 million shares worth $4.669 million, including around 10.68 million warrants in Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development Co.
Brokers said most investors were waiting for the listing of Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd on Tuesday, which could determine future short-term market direction.
"Despite the rise today, the market is still watching new market factors such as interim results," another broker said.
Of the 45 B share issues, 42 were traded with 22 of them gaining ground. Thirteen were lower while seven were unchanged.
Huaxin Cement was the star performer on speculative buying. It rose $0.010 or 7.69 percent to $0.140.

Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co topped the active list but ended unchanged at $0.434 on volume of 1.1 million shares. After the market close, it said its first-half net rose 147.7 percent from a year ago to 198 million yuan.

Shanghai Chlor Alkai Chemical Co was the second mostly actively traded issue on institutional buying amid talk of restructuring, brokers said. It rose $0.006 or 2.46 percent to $0.250 on volume of 750,348 shares.
Shanghai's A share index closed up on institutional buying, brokers said.
The A index gained 7.796 points or 0.62 percent to 1,256.271 points on volume of 400.7 million shares worth 4.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index shed 15.575 points or 0.42 percent to 3,727.361 points.
Newly listed Chongqing Three Gorges Water Conservancy and Electric Power Co Ltd surged on its first trading day, closing at 14.29 yuan compared with an issue price of 6.38 yuan.
Yizheng Chemical Fibre said government officials were studying a possible merger with other chemical firms. It was suspended in the morning but resumed later and finished up 0.03 yuan at 5.13 yuan.
Yizheng's H shares in Hong Kong were also buoyed by the statement. They gained HK$0.225 to HK$2.85.
